new.s: Who was the Buddhist monk with whom King Menander held the dialogue recorded in the Milindapanho?
new.x: The Milindapanho is a dialogue between King Milinda (Menander) and the Buddhist monk Nagasena.
new.angle: U0043 #2 Milindapanho -> monk in the dialogue

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Milindapanho:
1. It is written in Sanskrit.
2. It explains eight phases of agricultural work.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Milindapanho is in Pali, not Sanskrit; it also describes eight phases of agricultural work.
new.angle: U0043 #2 Milindapanho -> language of the text

new.s: Which deities are depicted on the coins of the Indo-Greek ruler Agathocles?
new.x: Agathocles issued coins showing Sankarshana (Balarama) and Vasudeva (Krishna).
new.angle: U0043 #3 Indo-Greek coinage -> deities depicted (Agathocles)

new.s: Which Indian symbol appears on the coins of Menander?
new.x: Menander, who turned Buddhist, issued coins with Indian symbols such as the Buddhist wheel.
new.angle: U0043 #1/#3 Menander -> coin feature (APPSC area: Indian symbols on coins)

new.s: Which is the first month of the Indian national calendar based on the Saka era?
new.x: The national calendar (from 22 March 1957) begins with Chaitra; 1 Chaitra falls on 22 March (21 March in a leap year).
new.angle: U0044 #5 Saka national calendar -> first month

new.s: Which inscription records the gift of a cave by Ayama, the minister of Nahapana, dated year 46?
new.x: Ayama, Nahapana's amatya, recorded the gift of a cave/mandapa at Junnar (Manmodi) in year 46.
new.angle: U0044 #1 Kshaharata inscription content -> inscription (PYQ yf3b9d5072e3 angle)

new.s: Which inscription records Rudradaman I's two victories over Satakarni and the repair of the Sudarshana lake?
new.x: The Junagadh (Girnar) inscription of Rudradaman I, dated Saka 72, records his victories over Satakarni and the repair of Sudarshana lake.
new.angle: U0044 #4 Junagadh inscription -> content (inscription named from its record)

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Satavahanas:
1. They were the first rulers to make tax-free land grants to Buddhists and Brahmanas.
2. They were the first dynasty to issue gold coins in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Satavahanas were the first to make tax-free land grants; the first gold coins in India were issued by the Indo-Greeks, and the Satavahanas issued no gold coins.
new.angle: U0047 PYQ y4ab823eabdf first tax-free land grants

new.s: Srisantamula, who defeated the Satavahana king Pulomavi III, founded which dynasty in Andhra?
new.x: Pulomavi III was defeated by the Ikshvaku Srisantamula, founder of the Ikshvaku line that followed the Satavahanas in Andhra.
new.angle: U0047 PYQ y9083dcff11d Ikshvaku founder (other direction)

new.s: Kotilingala in Karimnagar district is known for the coins of which Satavahana ruler?
new.x: Coins of the founder Simuka, with the legend 'Siri Chimuka Sata', have been found at Kotilingala in Telangana.
new.angle: U0047 #5/#10 PYQ yec704abd379 Kotilingala -> Simuka coins (other direction)

new.s: Which Purana, with the longest list of Satavahana kings, was compiled during the reign of Yajna Sri Satakarni?
new.x: The Matsya Purana gives the longest list (30 kings, 456 years) and was compiled in Yajna Sri Satakarni's reign.
new.angle: U0047 #3/#11 PYQ yddf5ad5e18d Purana -> period of compilation (other direction)

new.s: Which ruler of Kalinga sent his army to the west ignoring his contemporary, the Satavahana king Satakarni I?
new.x: The Hathigumpha inscription records that Kharavela of Kalinga sent an army west, ignoring his contemporary Satakarni I.
new.angle: U0047 #3 PYQ y5a5ab1ea9e8 Kharavela -> contemporary Satakarni I (other direction)

new.s: Apart from the Hathigumpha inscription, which text records the contact between Kalinga and the Satavahanas?
new.x: The Chulakalinga Jataka and the Hathigumpha inscription record the Kalinga contact in the time of Kharavela and Satakarni I.
new.angle: U0047 #3 Chulakalinga Jataka -> Kharavela conflict

new.s: Which river is called Kanhabenna in the Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela?
new.x: Kanhabenna is the Hathigumpha name for the Krishna river, to which Kharavela sent his army.
new.angle: U0047 #3 Hathigumpha -> Kharavela's campaign towards the Satavahanas

new.s: Who was the 30th king in the Matsya Purana list of Satavahana rulers?
new.x: In the Puranic list Pulomavi III is the 30th king; Gautamiputra was the 23rd and Hala the 17th.
new.angle: U0047 #7/#11 PYQ yadbce3a109e / y5e348a4766d last king in the Puranic list

new.s: The Karle inscription of Vasishthiputra Pulumavi records the gift of a village for the maintenance of which group of Buddhist monks?

new.angle: U0047 #9 PYQ y4a1cd5d769a Karle donation -> monks (other direction)

new.s: Simuka, the founder of Satavahana rule, issued coins bearing which legend?

new.angle: U0048 PYQ y891bb359e54 / y28c1ab6169e founder Simuka

new.s: The Nasik inscription of Ushavadatta records a deposit of 2,000 karshapanas with the guild of which craftsmen at Govardhana?

new.angle: U0048 #6/#17 PYQ y037c34fcec4 / y0744fc0bc70 Nasik inscription -> guild deposit (other direction)

new.s: Under which dynasty did Motupalli rise as a port?

new.angle: U0048 #22 PYQ ye40e58b0451 port -> period (Motupalli)

new.s: Which administrative unit was run by the Amatya in Satavahana administration?
new.x: The Amatya was the minister or district officer who ran the Aharas (districts).
new.angle: U0048 #12 PYQ y50e78308818 Ahara -> head officer (other direction)

new.s: To whom did the Satavahanas make the first tax-free land grants in Indian history?
new.x: The Satavahanas made the first tax-free land grants (agraharas) to Brahmanas and Buddhist monks, with immunities.
new.angle: U0048 #5/#14 tax-free land grants -> FIRST evidence

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Satavahana coinage?
o: Lead was the most commonly used metal
Coin legends were in Prakrit and Brahmi
Iron coins with a thin copper coating were issued
new.x: Iron coins with a thin copper coating belong to the Ikshvakus, not the Satavahanas.
new.angle: U0048 #18 coinage metals not used (iron coins with copper coating)

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Indo-Roman trade:
1. Roman trade peaked under the Satavahanas.
2. Roman trade flourished further after the Satavahanas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Roman trade peaked in the Satavahana period (1st c. BCE-3rd c. CE) and declined after them.
new.angle: U0048 #19/N1 PYQ yf7c2c6993fe fate of Roman trade after the Satavahanas

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. No ruler after the Satavahanas issued ship-motif coins.
2. The Phanigiri pot of lead coins belongs to the Ikshvakus.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Ship-motif coins ended with the Satavahanas; the Phanigiri pot of 3,730 lead coins is Ikshvaku.
new.angle: U0048 N1 coinage by successor dynasties (ship-motif, lead)
